To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Fd-Gogat is dual targeted and interacts physically with SHM1, and that this interaction is necessary to maintain photorespiratory serine hydroxyl methyltransferase activity.
Arabidopsis Fd-GOGAt interacts with mitochondrial SHMT1, that this interaction is required for photorespiratoy SHMT activity, and that this interaction is essential for the photorespiratory pathway.
the dual-targeted Fd-GOGat protein interacts with the SHMT protein to form a complex that is required for the photorespiratory conversion of glycine to serine in the mitochondria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Fd-GOGAt in photorespiration and nitrogen metabolism and the interaction between these two pathways.
the role of the photorespiratory pathway in plant metabolism.
the regulation of the photorespiratory pathway in plants and the role of protein–protein complexes in this regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Arabidopsis photorespiratory serine hydroxyl-methyl transferase activity requires the mitochondrial accumulation of ferredoxin-dependent glutamate synthase.
Arabidopsis SHMT1 requires Fd-GOGT to function in the mitochondria, which is necessary to complete the photorespiratory pathway.
Arabidopsis Fd-GOGAt is required for SHMT1-dependent photorespiratory activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Arabidopsis photorespiratory pathway is more complex than previously anticipated, and the regulation of the photorespiratory flux through SHMT requires the dual targeting and interaction of Fd-GOGat with SHMT1 in the mitochondria.
the Arabidopsis SHMT1 protein is not only a key player in the photorespiratory process but is also required to maintain the Fd-GOGAt protein in the mitochondria.
the photorespiratory serine hydroxyl methyl transferase activity requires the mitochondrial accumulation of Fd-GOGAt.
The main takeaway from our work is that
photorespiratory metabolism requires a high degree of coordination between chloroplastic and mitochondrial metabolism.
the mitochondrial accumulation of Fd-GOGat is necessary for SHMT activity and, thus, photorespiratory carbon metabolism.
Fd-GOAT is dual targeted, that it interacts with SHMT1 in the mitochondria, and that this interaction is necessary to support photorespiratory serine hydroxylmethyltransferase activity.
